questions.text: Explain the functions of the Supreme Court.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the functions of the Supreme Court. (Average )

answer.value:
Functions of the Supreme Court
The Supreme Court settles disputes between the Union and the States, and among the States.
It issues various writs to protect the Fundamental Rights of citizens.
It interprets the Constitution.
It gives advisory opinions to the President when sought.
It frames necessary rules and regulations.

questions.text: How has the Lok Adalat (People's Court) helped in preventing delays in the delivery of justice?
questions.text_as_printed: How has the Lok Adalat (People's Court) helped in preventing delays in the delivery of justice? (Difficult )

answer.value:
Role of Lok Adalat (People's Court)
Lok Adalat is a system established by the Government to settle disputes quickly, amicably, and at a low cost.
It is organized periodically at State and District levels.
Its award has the same legal status as a court decree.
The decision of a Lok Adalat is final and binding on both parties, thereby avoiding further expense, loss, and delay.

questions.text: What are the functions of the High Court?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the functions of the High Court? (Average )

answer.value:
High Court
The High Court is the highest court in a State.
It consists of the Chief Justice and other Judges.
The President of India appoints the Chief Justice after consultation with the Chief Justice of India and the Governor of the State.
The retirement age of a High Court Judge is 62 years.
Proceedings in the High Court may be conducted in English or the State's official language.
